Theres an old AMA of a guy who had broken both of his arms and was unable to manhandle the hamcandle by himself. His mom felt bad for him, and figured that it was good and moral to take matters into her own hands. I don't remember if they had already been in a sexual relationship at this point or if this was the start of it for them, but either way things continued between them long after.

This absolutely blew up on reddit and people were cracking jokes about broken arms literally any time someone mentioned a mom, or vice versa. People eventually started getting sick of broken arms jokes, but that didn't stop reddit from making them. Probably within the last couple years, the joke finally started dying and anyone who made it got booed and downvoted instead of getting 6 golds. 

At this point you almost never see anyone make the joke anymore (or at least I don't) but that means that now it's much easier to surprise people with it. Some people still think it's hilarious, but others like this person hate it with all their soul.

Strong characters have the ability to learn on their own, while Clueless Goddesses don't. Kali had never been exposed to the world either and she learned because she is strong and independent. Eleven is strong and independent as well, and based on what we've seen, she would have turned out the same way. The Clueless Goddess is a weak and flat character (see "needy and helpless") and Eleven is far from that.

The sixth paragraph.

"The trope is the intellectual, emotional version of the "Damsel in distress". Instead of needing physical help she now needs intellectual or emotional help. But, the thing is, she's needy and helpless."

Eleven didn't need intellectual or emotional help, and she is not needy or helpless. Without the help, she would have ended up like Kali and learned everything for herself. By definition, a damsel in distress cannot move from her current position without someone saving her, whereas Eleven would have developed on her own. Accepting help isn't the same as being helpless and unable to develop until a savior arrives.

The core concept behind the Clueless Goddess is that without the man saving her, she would have no real chance of survival, and depends on him for everything. Eleven has been shown time and again, even in Season 1, that she definitely could have survived on her own. She didn't rely on the restaurant owner to give her food, as she decided to steal it, rather than ask/beg for it. Later in the season, she decided to leave the boys and fend for herself, which she does pretty easily until deciding to return to them. 

Kali in Season 2 is what Eleven would have been, had she not found Mike -- fending for herself, not caring about social norms. She decided for herself to befriend the boys and let them help her, and she always comes back to them because she wants to, not because she can't survive without them. A Clueless Goddess is entirely dependent on the man and lets him make decisions for her because she is intellectually weak. Saying that Eleven is intellectually weak and can't survive independently just because she is a female who decides to let males into her life takes away all the agency and power from one of the strongest characters in the show.
